# Loyalty to the Older Truths Is the First Principle

Failure to take account of[^1] the part played by the older truths[^2] is the source of much of the unjust criticism leveled against pragmatism.[^3] Their influence is absolutely controlling.[^4] Loyalty to them is the first principle--in most cases it is the only principle; for by far the most usual way of handling phenomena so novel that they would make for a serious rearrangement of our preconceptions is to ignore them altogether, or to abuse those who bear witness for them.[^5]

[^1]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Formation of New Beliefs]] "Failure to take account of"
[^2]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Formation of New Beliefs]] "the part played by the older truths"
[^3]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Formation of New Beliefs]] "is the source of much of the unjust criticism leveled against pragmatism."
[^4]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Formation of New Beliefs]] "Their influence is absolutely controlling."
